steps.title: What is a Vertical Gauge?
steps.markdown:
A **Vertical Gauge** is a live bar indicator that tracks a single numeric value from any datasource.

It supports:
- Configurable min / max range and engineering units
- Colour-coded alarm zones (warning and critical)
- A **runtime offset** control that lets you shift the reading up or down without editing settings

In this tutorial you will connect a gauge to a built-in signal generator and explore the offset control.

steps.title: Add a signal generator
steps.markdown:
A **Signal Generator** datasource produces a continuous synthetic waveform — no hardware needed.

1. Open the **Datasources** side panel and click **Add datasource**.
2. Select **Signal Generator** from the picker.
3. Leave the default settings (sine wave, amplitude 1, offset 0) and click **OK**.

The datasource will start producing values in the range −1 to 1.

steps.title: Create a pane
steps.markdown:
Every widget lives inside a **pane**.

Click the **Add pane** button in the top bar.

steps.title: Add a Vertical Gauge widget
steps.markdown:
Click the **Add widget** icon on the pane, then select **Vertical Gauge** from the widget picker.

Enter a title (e.g. `My Signal`) in the settings dialog and click **OK**.

steps.title: Connect the gauge to your signal
steps.markdown:
Click the **wrench (edit)** icon on the gauge widget to open its editor.

In the **Source** section:
1. Click the datasource dropdown and select your signal generator.
2. In the **Display** section set **Min** to `-1` and **Max** to `1`.
3. Click **Save**.

The gauge bar will now track the live sine wave.

steps.title: Explore runtime offset
steps.markdown:
The gauge widget has **+** and **−** buttons at the bottom labelled *offset*.

Click **+** or **−** to shift the displayed reading up or down without changing the datasource or saving any settings.

This is useful for zeroing a sensor or applying a known calibration correction at runtime.

steps.title: Tutorial complete
steps.markdown:
Your Vertical Gauge is live and you have explored the runtime offset control.

**What you learned:**
- How to add a Signal Generator datasource
- How to add and configure a Vertical Gauge widget
- How to bind a gauge to a datasource via the integrated editor
- How the runtime offset shifts readings without touching settings

Close this panel with **Done** and explore the other tutorials.
